properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 18 at 10:30AM MDT until September 19 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Pocatello ID
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, eastern, and southeast Idaho,
including the following areas, in central Idaho, Challis/Pahsimeroi
Valleys, Frank Church Wilderness, Lost River Valley,
Sawtooth/Stanley Basin, Sun Valley Region and Wood River Foothills.
In eastern Idaho, Beaverhead - Lemhi Highlands, Big Hole Mountains,

Idaho, Arco/Mud Lake Desert, Bear Lake Valley, Bear River Range,
Blackfoot Mountains, Caribou Range, Franklin/Eastern Oneida Region,
Lower Snake River Plain and Marsh and Arbon Highlands.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,

evening across central and eastern Idaho. Rainfall amounts in
excess of 0.50" are possible, leading to flooding within burn
scars, steep terrain, and urban areas.

properties.areaDesc: Upper Chena River Valley; Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 18 at 4:31AM AKDT until September 19 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Including the following areas, Fairbanks, North Pole, Two
Rivers, Fort Wainwright, Ester, and Fox

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rain may result in minor flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The Chena River is running higher than normal and will continue
to be high through the week. As of 4 AM AKDT Friday, river levels
near the Upper Chena have crested and are beginning to come down.
The Chena below Hunts Creek is still rising gradually but
beginning to level off. The Chena below Moose Creek Dam is also
rising still. Water levels on the Little Chena are still
gradually rising but it will be cresting soon as the rate of rise
has dropped off. Peak water levels near Moose Creek Dam will
likely be tonight through Saturday.

- This means low-lying and typical flood-prone areas may
experience areas of flooding through the end of the week as water
levels gradually rise then fall. In addition, other creeks and
streams in the vicinity will be running at elevated levels.

- For more updated river information, please refer to
water.noaa.gov or weather.gov/aprfc
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor the latest forecasts and be alert for possible
Flood Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be
prepared to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 18 at 3:08AM MDT until September 19 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of west central and northwest New Mexico as well
as the South Central Mountains and Eastern Lincoln County. This
includes the Ruidoso area burn scars.

* WHEN...From noon MDT today through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Soils are very saturated from days of soaking rainfall. Rainfall
rates of 1 to 1.5 inches per hour may occur with storms Friday
afternoon and evening. Wildfire burn scars, urban areas,
communities with underdeveloped infrastructure, complex terrain,
and areas where the ground is already saturated are most at risk
for rapid runoff and flash flooding. Storms across western New
Mexico will end during the evening, but storms could persist as
late as Midnight in the Lincoln County portion of the Watch.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 18 at 2:50AM MDT until September 20 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Billings MT
properties.description:
A strong and slow moving weather system will impact the region
tonight through Sunday. Well above normal atmospheric moisture levels
combined with the dynamics from this storm system will provide the
potential for heavy rainfall during this period. Thunderstorms
embedded in the more general rainfall will have the potential to
produce flash flooding, particularly over recent burn scars.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible, along
with Flash Flooding of recent burn scars.

* WHERE...All of South Central Montana, Portions of Southeast
Montana, and Sheridan County Wyoming.

* WHEN...From this evening through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of creeks and
other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in
poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1 to 2.5 inches of rainfall is expected across the watch area
tonight through Sunday. Locally heavier totals up to 4 inches are
possible where thunderstorm activity is more persistent.
- The Robertson Draw, East Side, Elk, and McGhee-Remington burn
scars are particularly vulnerable to Flash Flooding and debris
flows during the watch period. Any other burn scars from this
summer will have elevated Flash Flood potential as well.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Please monitor forecasts and be alert for possible Flood Warnings.
Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared to take
action should flooding develop.
